values.note: Lower Elkhorn NRD: every electric pad $25 a night; tents off the pads $10 per tent; overflow camping in the north lots $10. No park permit or entrance fee.

fees.source: https://www.lenrd.org/maskenthine-lake-recreation-area (Camper Fee: 'All Electric pads-30 amp (110 volts), 50 amp (120 volts), & 20 amp $25', 'Overflow camping in north lots $10'; 'No park permit or fee is required for entrance'; page (c) 2026), read 2026-11-04

values.note: Shower house water is on from about May 1 to October 1, weather permitting.

facilities.source: https://www.lenrd.org/maskenthine-lake-recreation-area ('A shower house is also available for Maskenthine campers ... with shower stalls, sinks and restrooms. Water is turned on from approximately May 1 until October 1st - weather permitting'), read 2026-11-04

values.note: Camper pads book on the NRD's Firefly page up to 60 days ahead; some pads stay first-come, and the tent area is first-come. The portal takes reservations from May 1 on; before that the campground is first-come only ('Campground is open through April 30th on a first-come first-served basis'). Weekends need Friday and Saturday; Memorial Day weekend needs Friday, Saturday and Sunday (the only holiday the portal names).

booking.source: https://app.fireflyreservations.com/reserve/property/MaskenthineRecreationArea ('Reservations can only be made up to 60 days in advance of departure date. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days. Minimum stay for Memorial Day weekend is Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. All other weekends have a minimum stay of Friday and Saturday'; 'Grey - First-Come First-Served (not reservable)') + https://www.lenrd.org/maskenthine-lake-recreation-area ('The camper pads can now be reserved 60 days in advance of arrival. Some sites are still first-come, first-served'), read 2026-11-04

note: Lower Elkhorn NRD recreation area around a 100-acre flood-control lake, 10 mi east of Norfolk near Stanton; fishing, no-wake boating, swim beach, disc golf, mountain-bike trails, arboretum. The 33 electric camper pads sit on a loop near the swimming beach, 70-100 m from the shore across a mowed lawn and a tree line. Tent area first-come. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the NRD page and its Firefly booking page: $25 electric pads (20/30/50 amp), 33 pads, shower house with restrooms, 60-day window, some pads first-come, 14-night limit; added 50-amp, flush toilets, the Firefly link, and the weekend 2-night / Memorial Day 3-night minimums. Not stated: water/sewer at pads, dump, campground season. Waterfront stays not waterfront. Note cleaned.
flags: Waterfront (no change, confirmed down): imagery shows the camper loop's east-side pads 70-100 m from the lake edge, across a wide mowed lawn with a tree line and a reed/shrub fringe along the shore; the loop road runs between too. Not on the water; I could not see a clear lake view from the pads through the trees, so not waterfront stays.
Pin: stored 41.98016,-97.23997 is the entrance-road junction north-west of the camper loop, ~220 m from the loop's centre (41.9790,-97.2378). Just under the 250 m line; move if wanted.
Phone 402-371-7313 is the NRD office (matches entry; also the Firefly page's reservation phone).

Season: not stated for the campground. The Firefly page says it 'is open through April 30th on a first-come first-served basis' with reservations from May 1, which reads as open year-round, but no page says so outright; left unset.
